name: Real-Time Provider Health
tagline: The best provider won't stay the best.
brief: Provider A is best — until it goes offline mid-run. Route so the queue keeps clearing after it drops.
context: A is cheap and reliable at first, then goes offline partway through. B is steady the whole time.
narrative: The starter rule assumes Provider A is always the best and hardcodes it. That holds for the first few payments — then A goes offline and every payment sent to it fails. A real routing engine watches live health and adapts. Route so that when A is down, the queue keeps moving through B.
objective: Process every payment with at most one failure as provider health changes.
learningObjective: Continuous decisions: re-decide every tick from live state instead of committing to one plan.
intelligenceExplanation: The provider cards update every tick. A is the preferred provider while it is online, then it drops. Put the live A rule above the B fallback so the agent changes route only when A is unavailable.
hint: Put WHEN onlineA → route-a above WHEN onlineB → route-b.
hints: Watch Provider A's card — it goes offline partway through the run.
A fixed 'always route A' rule can't adapt. Use a live condition: WHEN onlineA → DO route-a.
Put WHEN onlineB → DO route-b underneath it, so B takes over after A drops.

steps.label: At most one failed payment through the health change

rules.description: Naive: always route to A (breaks when A goes offline).

functions.description: Send the payment through Provider A.
Send the payment through Provider B.
